record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Local stability of endemic equilibria for SIR-PH variants
record.original_question: For SIR-PH epidemic models and their SIR-PH-FA and SIR-PH-IA approximations with linear births, vaccination, loss of immunity, and disease-induced mortality, does R0>1 always imply local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium whenever such a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium exists?

evidence.quote: However, the second property, the sufficiency of R0 > 1 for the local stability of an endemic point, remains open even for SIR-PH-FA models, despite the numerous particular cases in which it was checked to hold (via Routh-Hurwitz time-onerous computations, or Lyapunov functions).
Remark 8 We conjecture that the endemic point is always locally stable when 1 < R0.

However, the check of the sum of the second and third order principal leading minors of the Jacobian at
EE, and of the additional Hurwitz criterion, seemed to exceed our machine power.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a SIR-PH epidemic model defined as follows. Let the population be split into a susceptible compartment $S$, a vector of "disease" (infectious/exposed) compartments $\mathbf{I}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ governed by a phase-type structure, and a removed compartment $R$. The disease compartments follow $\dot{\mathbf{I}} = (\boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{I})\,S\,\boldsymbol{\alpha} + \mathbf{I}^\top A$, where $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ with $\sum_i\alpha_i=1$ is the initial distribution among disease states, $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ is a vector of infection rates, and $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is a sub-generator (Markovian transition matrix among disease states with absorption). The full SIR-PH system also incorporates:
- a linear birth rate (constant inflow into $S$),
- natural mortality at rate $\mu>0$ for every compartment,
- vaccination of susceptibles (transferring mass into $R$) and loss of immunity (transferring mass from $R$ into $S$),
- disease-induced mortality from the $\mathbf{I}$ compartments (an extra removal rate vector $\boldsymbol{\nu}\ge 0$),
- vaccination-induced mortality.

Define the basic reproduction number $R_0$ via the next-generation matrix construction of van den Driessche and Watmough applied to this model. A disease-free equilibrium (DFE) is an equilibrium with $\mathbf{I}=0$; an endemic equilibrium (EE) is an equilibrium with $\mathbf{I}\ne 0$ whose coordinates are biologically feasible (all non-negative).

Consider also two simplifications used in the literature:
- The SIR-PH-FA approximation, in which the total population is replaced by its equilibrium value in the force-of-infection term (frequency-dependent transmission with fixed total population $N$).
- The SIR-PH-IA approximation, an "incidence approximation" obtained by linearizing certain mass-action terms around the DFE.

Question. Is the following statement true: for every SIR-PH model (and likewise for every SIR-PH-FA and SIR-PH-IA approximation) with parameters as above, whenever $R_0>1$ and a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium exists, that endemic equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that $R_0>1$ implies local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium for SIR-PH models (and their FA/IA approximations) is stated explicitly as an open problem. It has been verified in numerous special cases via Routh–Hurwitz or Lyapunov methods, but no general proof or counterexample appears to have been published; subsequent literature on SIR-PH models still treats it as conjectural.

status_evidence.title: New Results and Open Questions for SIR-PH Epidemic Models
status_evidence.snippet: The sufficiency of R0 > 1 for the local stability of an endemic point remains open even for SIR-PH-FA models, despite numerous particular cases in which it was checked to hold.
status_evidence.claim: Local stability of the endemic equilibrium under R0>1 for SIR-PH-type models is stated as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A look at endemic equilibria of compartmental epidemiological models
status_evidence.snippet: It is generally impossible to find general laws concerning endemic points, though commonly when R0>1 a unique endemic point exists.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of endemic-equilibrium stability across compartmental classes lacks a unified theorem.
